leases.summary: Pinned PG18.6 container lifecycle via podman CLI (ensure/status/drift/restart/exec_psql).
leases.spec: Implement every NotImplementedError body per the module docstring. All podman calls go through self.runner (injectable) with argv lists, never shell strings. status(): parse `podman container inspect <name>` JSON (a list with one object); missing container -> exit code non-zero + 'no such container' in stderr. drift(): compare ImageDigest with config.PG_IMAGE_DIGEST, published host port, and that every spec.mounts container path appears in Mounts[].Destination. ensure(): follow the state machine in the docstring exactly; never touch a container named 'pgarbor-oracle'. wait_ready(): two consecutive successful `pg_isready` + `psql -c 'select 1'` probes 1 s apart. Tests (harness/tests/test_har_01.py, pytest, NO podman): a FakeRunner recording argv and returning canned CompletedProcess objects; assert ContainerSpec.run_argv() exact list, ensure() issues run when missing, start when stopped, raises OracleError on drift without recreate.
acceptance: ContainerSpec().run_argv() starts with ['podman','run','-d','--name','pgarbor-harness-pg18','-p','127.0.0.1:54319:5432'] and contains the image digest exactly once
ensure() never invokes podman with the name 'pgarbor-oracle'
drift() reports a digest mismatch when inspect returns another ImageDigest
with podman available, ensure() yields an endpoint where SHOW server_version = '18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2)'

leases.summary: Pooled single oracle instance with per-case CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE isolation and global-object hygiene.
leases.spec: Implement OraclePool per the module docstring. psycopg is imported lazily inside methods (`import psycopg`), admin connection with autocommit=True. Quote database names with double quotes (names are generated, [a-z0-9_] only; assert that). start(): drop stale databases matching config.CASE_DB_PREFIX except config.CASE_TEMPLATE_DB using `SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datname LIKE 'pgarbor\_case\_%'` then DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE). acquire(): semaphore first, then CREATE DATABASE; on failure release the semaphore before raising. Endpoint gucs = tuple(sorted(config.DIFFERENTIAL_SESSION_GUCS.items())). Tests: unit-test case_db_name determinism and the semaphore bound with a fake admin_execute (monkeypatch); mark live tests @pytest.mark.oracle.
acceptance: case_db_name('smoke.x',1,123) is stable across runs and equals 'pgarbor_case_123_' + 10 hex chars
start() never drops a case database whose embedded pid is a live process
acquire() blocks when max_parallel databases are outstanding (fake admin)
release() always releases the semaphore even when DROP DATABASE raises
live: 8 concurrent acquire/release cycles leave no pgarbor_case_* databases except the template

leases.summary: Oracle fingerprint document, sha, and drift verification.
leases.spec: Implement collect/verify/verify_live exactly per docstring. Settings are read with `SELECT name, setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = ANY(%s)` — note pg_settings names are case-sensitive as listed in pg_settings (e.g. 'TimeZone', 'DateStyle'); for names not in pg_settings use current_setting(name). builtin_counts via count(*) of pg_type/pg_proc/pg_operator/pg_cast. verify(): one violation string per mismatch, format 'path: expected X, got Y'. Tests: verify() on a hand-built good document returns [], on documents with a wrong digest / TimeZone / locale returns the exact strings.
acceptance: fingerprint_sha256(doc) is stable under dict key reordering
verify(doc) == [] for a document built from the live pinned oracle
verify reports 'image_digest: expected sha256:7493..., got ...' on digest drift

leases.summary: PostgreSQL-lexical statement splitter, comment stripper, top-level ORDER BY detection, first keyword, message templates.
leases.spec: Write one small hand-rolled scanner (index loop over the string) shared by all functions, honoring: '...' with '' escapes, E'..' backslash escapes (E or e prefix immediately before the quote), "..." identifiers, $tag$..$tag$ dollar quotes (tag rule in docstring; '$' followed by digit is a parameter), -- comments, nested /* */ comments, parentheses depth, and BEGIN ATOMIC ... END nesting (psqlscan.l: count BEGIN/CASE vs END tokens only after seeing CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION/PROCEDURE ... BEGIN ATOMIC). Doctests in the docstrings must pass (run them in the test file with doctest.testmod). Read ~/develop/reference/postgres-18/src/fe_utils/psqlscan.l for the dollar-quote and BEGIN ATOMIC rules (reference only).

leases.summary: Exact libpq session driver over psycopg.pq (non-blocking, notices, COPY, cancel, timeouts).
leases.spec: Implement Session per docstring using ONLY psycopg.pq low-level API (lazy import). After `uv sync` (central), verify method names against .venv/lib/python3*/site-packages/psycopg/pq/abc.py; if a listed method differs, use the real one and note it in your submission assumptions. Set conn.nonblocking = 1 and drive every wait through select() with a deadline; call flush() until it returns 0 after each send_*. Notice handler: a closure appending model.Notice built from res.error_field(...) to self._notice_buffer; on step start move buffered notices into the step's list. Map pq.TransactionStatus to I/T/E/A/U. Values: text format decode('utf-8'); binary keep bytes. Parameters: None -> None; text -> str.encode(); binary -> bytes.fromhex(). Tests: pure unit tests of the PGresult->StatementResult conversion with a fake result object implementing the attributes; live tests (@pytest.mark.oracle) for multi-statement simple query, COPY TO STDOUT, prepare/describe/execute, async start/poll/finish of a pg_sleep(0.3).
acceptance: run_simple('select 1; select null::text, \'\'::text') yields 2 'rows' results with values [['1']] and [[None, '']]
an ErrorResponse yields kind 'error' with sqlstate, message, position as sent by the server
COPY (select 1) TO STDOUT yields one copy_out result with rows [['1\n']] and command_tag 'COPY 1'
a step exceeding step_timeout_s returns timed_out=True within step_timeout_s + 3 s and the session reconnects on next use

acceptance: an edit to tests/expected/** without a review record makes ok False
the same edit with a covering review record makes ok True
there is no parameter or env var that bypasses a violation
